reviewed_by: Delegated coding agent static review against live Binary Ninja 6.0.10601 MCP (retail PE view_1), radare2 6.2.0 CFG and angr 10.0.4.post1 CFGFast on retail igi.exe; candidate source read from this worktree. No game process was executed and no runtime behavior is claimed.
review_basis: Retail 0x004AA0A6 was re-disassembled, re-decompiled and re-CFG'd through the live Binary Ninja view, independently recovered with radare2 6.2.0 and angr 10.0.4.post1 CFGFast. The candidate is scripts/GameNatives/mathsys/004AA0A6-MathSys_Invoke19.cpp at sha256 204a77fef67d9e471479bbc88b5688cb7300c665dd6420a472dff3fea6563f00 (recorded implementation.signature: void* __convention MathSys_Invoke19("regparm")(int32_t param_1, char* param_2);). The evidence artifact digests are bound in this review.

retail_function.name: MathSys_Invoke19
retail_function.summary: 25 blocks / 35 edges across two BN ranges 0x4AA090-0x4AA095 and 0x4AA0A6-0x4AA15C: align EDX to 4, scan byte-wise for the character or NUL, then scan a dword at a time with the 0x7EFEFEFF haszero trick; on a hit compare the four bytes with AL/AH (cmp al,bl at 0x4AA11B, cmp ah,bl at 0x4AA123, shr 0x10 then cmp al,bl at 0x4AA12E and cmp ah,bl at 0x4AA136) and return EDX-1/-2/-3/-4; the shared epilogue is 0x4AA090 (lea eax,[edx-1]; pop ebx; ret) and 0x4AA114 returns 0.

candidate_function.summary: MathSys_Invoke19(int arg1, char* arg2) reproduces the alignment loop, the haszero scan and the six hit/NUL branches, but its per-byte comparisons are the decompiler's dword-typed forms `*(&eax_8 + 1) == ebx_3` and `*(&eax_9 + 1) == ebx_3`.

divergences: Per-byte hit checks use dword-typed expressions `*(&eax_8 + 1) == ebx_3` and `*(&eax_9 + 1) == ebx_3`; retail compares the byte registers (cmp al,bl at 0x4AA11B, cmp ah,bl at 0x4AA123, cmp al,bl at 0x4AA12E, cmp ah,bl at 0x4AA136). The candidate's comparisons therefore test the wrong width and offset.
The candidate also compares the first dword with `eax_8 == ebx_3` where retail compares only AL (0x4AA11B).
candidate_comparison.statement: Divergences are listed above; by contract they keep the record at TRANSCRIBED or lower.

checks.name: function_identity
checks.detail: Retail entry 0x004AA0A6 is recovered by all three tools; the address-bound implementation is scripts/GameNatives/mathsys/004AA0A6-MathSys_Invoke19.cpp (sha256 204a77fef67d9e471479bbc88b5688cb7300c665dd6420a472dff3fea6563f00). 25 blocks / 35 edges across two BN ranges 0x4AA090-0x4AA095 and 0x4AA0A6-0x4AA15C: align EDX to 4, scan byte-wise for the character or NUL, then scan a dword at a time with the 0x7EFEFEFF haszero trick; on a hit compare the four bytes with AL/AH (cmp al,bl at 0x4AA11B, cmp ah,bl at 0x4AA123, shr 0x10 then cmp al,bl at 0x4AA12E and cmp ah,bl at 0x4AA136) and return EDX-1/-2/-3/-4; the shared epilogue is 0x4AA090 (lea eax,[edx-1]; pop ebx; ret) and 0x4AA114 returns 0. Candidate: MathSys_Invoke19(int arg1, char* arg2) reproduces the alignment loop, the haszero scan and the six hit/NUL branches, but its per-byte comparisons are the decompiler's dword-typed forms `*(&eax_8 + 1) == ebx_3` and `*(&eax_9 + 1) == ebx_3`.

checks.name: abi_and_signature
checks.detail: Retail takes the character in EAX (BL) and the string at [E+4]; BN and the candidate both declare `void* __convention("regparm")(int32_t arg1, char* arg2 @ 0x4)`, so arg2 is the [E+4] slot and the register count matches.

checks.name: argument_mapping
checks.detail: arg1 (EAX) is the searched character, arg2 ([E+4]) is the string base; both are used in the same roles in the candidate.

checks.name: control_flow_shape
checks.detail: Binary Ninja and radare2 agree on 25 blocks / 35 edges (similarity 1.000); angr CFGFast recovers 25 blocks with has_unresolved_jumps=false.

checks.name: calls_and_side_effects
checks.detail: Leaf function; no calls in retail or candidate.

checks.name: constants_and_scaling
checks.detail: 0x7EFEFEFF, 0x81010100, 0x1010100, 0x80000000 and the 8/0x10 replication shifts all match.

checks.name: memory_layout_and_access
checks.detail: Retail's byte-hit checks read the byte registers (AL/AH) of the dword at [EDX-4]. The candidate's `*(&eax_8 + 1)` / `*(&eax_9 + 1)` are int/uint16 pointer expressions: as written they address +4 and +2 bytes and compare a wider value against the replicated dword ebx_3, so the compared width/offset does not match the retail `cmp al,bl` / `cmp ah,bl` instructions.

checks.name: return_and_error_paths
checks.detail: All return paths are present: EDX-1/-2/-3/-4 on a hit and NULL when the scan reaches a NUL.

signature_comparison.rationale: Binary Ninja reports "void* __convention("regparm")(int32_t arg1, char* arg2 @ 0x4)" at 0x004AA0A6; radare2 recovers "fcn.004aa0a6 (int32_t arg_8h);". Both tools place the entry at 0x004AA0A6 and agree on the stack/register word count and cleanup; the difference is the level of type/argument-name detail, not the call frame. Candidate declaration: void* __convention MathSys_Invoke19("regparm")(int32_t param_1, char* param_2);.

limitations: No game process was executed; this review is static (live Binary Ninja, radare2 CFG, angr CFGFast) plus the candidate source.
The candidate defines MathSys_Invoke19; the catalog name is a harvest label for a strchr-shaped CRT helper, not a game routine.

The record entry is 0x4AA0A6, but BN also reports a 5-byte shared epilogue range at 0x4AA090 and a separate 6-byte adaptor entry at 0x4AA0A0 (xor eax,eax; mov al,[esp+8]) which falls into the entry; neither is covered by the candidate.
